title: Indemnity & Data Responsibility — brain dump
content:
Notes to self — high level priorities:
- Protect Redwood from third-party IP claims tied to vendor-delivered models or embeddings.
- Keep vendor indemnity narrow but meaningful: third-party IP infringement and data breaches caused by vendor negligence. Avoid vague open-ended indemnities.
- Cap liability but preserve carveouts for willful misconduct, gross negligence, and IP indemnity (we may want a separate sub-cap or no cap for IP?).
- Ensure breach notification timelines and forensics cooperation; include obligation to notify within 48 hours of detection (we usually ask 24–48).
- Subprocessors / subcontractors: require prior notice for new subprocessors and right to object for sensitive categories (on-prem, gov data).
- Escrow: in high-risk deals (enterprise, regulated), require source/weights/config escrow or at least model artifacts + documented reproducible process.
- Export controls / sanctions: affirmative covenant that vendor complies and will not provide service in sanctioned jurisdictions.
- Audit rights: limit to once per year, business hours, with reasonable scope/notice; avoid unlimited forensic audits that disrupt ops.

Redline checklist (quick):
1) Indemnity scope: propose vendor indemnifies Redwood against third-party claims alleging: (a) IP infringement by vendor deliverables, (b) breaches of confidentiality or data protection obligations, (c) regulatory fines arising solely from vendor misconduct.
   - language to propose: "Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Redwood from all third-party claims arising out of Vendor Materials infringing any U.S. or EEA patent, copyright, trade secret, or trademark, provided Redwood gives prompt notice and cooperates."
   - limit: require vendor to cover costs of defense & settlement; Redwood retains right to participate in defense with counsel of choice at our cost.
2) Carveouts from cap: insist that IP indemnity and intentional misconduct are not subject to the general liability cap. If they push back, propose higher sub-cap (e.g., 3x fees) for IP.
3) Liability cap: propose cap = lesser of (a) 12 months of paid fees under the order, or (b) $5M. Typical vendors push lower; we can trade on contract length/enterprise value.
4) Data breach: vendor to indemnify for costs from unauthorized access arising from vendor negligence. Include credit for vendor's insurance and obligation to maintain cyber liability policy ($5M) and provide certificate on request.
5) Notification & remediation: require notification "without undue delay" but we push for 48 hours after discovery. Vendor to provide root cause analysis within 14 days and remediation plan within 30 days.
6) Subprocessor clause: prior notice + 10 business day objection window for new subprocessors processing customer data. If we object, allow termination or require vendor to remove/replace subprocessor.
7) Escrow: ask for model artifacts + deployment instructions in escrow, released upon vendor bankruptcy or prolonged force majeure > 90 days.
8) Audit rights: limited, require redaction safeguards, 30 days notice, scope limited to data protection and compliance, use designated third-party auditor with NDA.

Negotiation talking points (short):
- Counterparty worry: they will resist uncapped IP indemnity and long breach timelines.
- Our leverage: customer size, potential to buy Dedicated or Private (we can treat bigger customers differently), we can accept sub-cap or require insurance if they refuse unlimited IP.
- Trade-offs we can make: shorter breach notification (48 vs 24) in exchange for stronger indemnity language; accept 12-month fee cap if we get IP carveout and higher cyber insurance requirement.
- Escrow is a negotiation sweet spot: ask for it in enterprise deals; for hosted API customers try to offer alternative (periodic reproducible artifact snapshots + attestations) to avoid vendor pushback.

Draft redline snippets to copy/paste:
- Indemnity: "Vendor shall, at its sole cost and expense, defend Redwood against any claim that Vendor Materials infringe a third party's intellectual property rights and shall pay all costs finally awarded against Redwood in connection with such claim (including reasonable attorneys' fees) or any amounts agreed in settlement in Vendor's sole discretion. This obligation is contingent on Redwood providing prompt written notice, reasonable cooperation, and sole control of the defense (subject to Redwood's right to participate)."
- Data breach notification: "Vendor shall notify Redwood without undue delay and in any event within forty-eight (48) hours after Vendor becomes aware of a security incident affecting Redwood Data. Vendor shall provide a root cause analysis within fourteen (14) days and a remediation plan within thirty (30) days."
- Subprocessor notice: "Vendor will provide written notice at least ten (10) business days prior to engaging any new subprocessor that will process Customer Data and will permit Customer to object for reasonable security or compliance grounds; if Customer objects, Vendor will use commercially reasonable efforts to make available a change in the services to avoid the use of the objected subprocessor."
- Escrow: "Upon execution of the Order, Vendor shall deposit copies of Model Artifacts and deployment instructions into an independent escrow agent. Escrow shall be released to Redwood upon Vendor insolvency, cessation of service for a period exceeding ninety (90) consecutive days, or material breach by Vendor that is not cured within sixty (60) days."

Tactical notes / playbook items:
- If they push for broad indemnity including customer claims: push back — our goal is vendor-only faults; exclude claims arising from our use of outputs in ways not contemplated in the SOW.
- If they demand liability cap alignment with fees only: insist on carveouts for IP and gross negligence.
- Insurance: require evidence of cyber liability + E&O; ask for 30-day notice of material changes or cancellation.
- Data residency ask: if vendor will process EU personal data, require Standard Contractual Clauses or equivalent and register subprocessors processing EU data.
- For open-source model components: require vendor to disclose OSS components and confirm compliance with licenses (esp. copyleft like AGPL). If AGPL present, escalate — high friction.

Open questions to resolve before senior sign-off:
- Do we accept sub-cap for IP if vendor refuses uncapped? If so, what number (suggest 3x annual fees or $10M, whichever is lower)?
- For Hosted API customers processing regulated data, do we require escrow? Or can we operationalize a "rapid model export" playbook instead?
- What's the minimum cyber insurance payout we will accept for top-tier enterprise (suggest $10M)? For smaller customers maybe $5M.

Quick references (links to my notes / past redlines):
- Confluence page: CONFLUENCE-LEGAL-1234 (model indemnity templates)
- Jira: JIRA-SEC-987 (open security exceptions)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prs/456 (example escrow clause in managed offering)

Action items:
- Sync with Ravi on acceptable IP sub-cap thresholds by EOD Friday.
- Add Sofia to thread to confirm breach notification/forensics SLAs we can operationally support.
- Draft two negotiation playbooks: one for SMB-hosted deals (more flexible, lower escrow expectation), one for enterprise/private (strict escrow, higher insurance, no IP cap).

Random sticky thoughts (notes to self that might be useful later):
- Consider a separate narrowly-tailored "model IP warranty" instead of broad indemnity for delivered models: vendor warrants it owns/has rights to supply model and won't knowingly include third-party licensed models. Easier to push.
- For open-source dependencies, ask for a BOM and attestation that no incompatible copyleft is embedded.
- If vendor refuses escrow entirely, require regular signed attestations + reproducible training logs + a time-limited grace for emergency fallback (e.g., interim API access on read-only export).

End of brain dump. Keep this informal — will drafted into a template for negotiations next week.
